For Respondents 1 & 3 : Ms. Sameeksha Gupta,
Panel Lawyer.
Hon'ble

Mr. Justice Naresh Kumar Chandravanshi Order On Board 09-01-2024 Heard.
1.

This petition has not been preferred against any particular order, rather it has been preferred against inaction on the part of respondent authorities and for direction to the respondents for initiation of proceeding and for deciding the applications under Section 73 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (henceforth "Act of 2023") filed by the petitioners within a specific time frame.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would submit that the petitioners are owners of various respective lands situated at village Gopalpur, Tehsil Dabhra, District Sakti, CG.

It is further submitted that lands of the petitioners were acquired for construction of Kalma Bairaj vide award dated 2-6-2021 passed in Land Acquisition Case No. 12/A-82/2016-17 by the Land Acquisition Officer - cum-Sub Divisional Officer (Revenue), Dabhra, Distt. Janjgir - Champa (Now Shakti).

Subsequently, on the application preferred by one Sukhiram, Reference Case No. 26/2023 was registered, in which award dated 10-10-2023 was passed in his favour by the Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority and award amount, granted to him, has been enhanced,
thereafter, the petitioners on instant petitioon have also moved their respective applications (Annexure P-1 colly.) before Collector, District Shakti under Section 73 of the Act of 2013, but the same have not been considered by the Collector till date.

Hence, it is prayed by counsel for the petitioner that this petition may be disposed of directing respondent No. 3 - Collector, Shakti to consider and decide the respective applications (Annexure P-1 colly.) filed by the petitioners within the period specified by this Court.

Dular vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 9 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119767273/
3 3.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State would submit that applications / representations (Annexure P-1 colly.) have been filed by the petitioners recently and only two months have been passed.
She further submits that respondent No. 3 / Collector is obliged to consider and decide the aforesaid applications /representations of the petitioners in accordance.
She further submits that considering the limited prayer made by the petitioners, she has no objection in allowing the prayer.

4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, it is found that no much period has been elapsed after filing of applications / representations filed by respective petitioners and State Counsel submits that the same are under consideration before the Collector, Shakti.
5.

Considering aforesaid facts and limited prayer made by learned counsel for the petitioners,
respondent No. 3 - Collector, Shakti is directed to consider and decide the applications/
representation (Annexure P-1 colly.) filed by the respective petitioners, within a period of 90 days from the date of receipt / submission of a copy of this order in accordance with law.

The petitioners may also file copy of their respective applications / representations before the concerned Collector,
if required.
6. With the aforesaid observations & directions, this writ petition stands disposed of at the motion stage itself.
7. It is made clear this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of case.

Sd/-
(Naresh Kumar Chandravanshi) Judge Amit/-
